evals.prompt: Google Play rejected our Data safety form. We use Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics. Can we just say no data is shared?
evals.expected_output: Do not assume SDK behavior. Inspect actual SDK versions/configuration and current Google disclosures, trace collection and sharing, then reconcile the Data safety form and privacy policy. Identify unanswered data flows rather than declaring compliance from the SDK names.

evals.prompt: Our Android app uses background location, SMS permissions, and a foreground service. Will Google Play approve it?
evals.expected_output: Inspect the merged manifest and real feature use, then check current eligibility, declarations, prominent disclosure/consent, foreground service types, and review evidence for each sensitive API. Do not assume manifest declarations guarantee approval or give a blanket yes/no.

evals.prompt: Play suspended our developer account. Write an appeal saying it was a mistake.
evals.expected_output: First obtain the full notice, policy citation, scope, deadline, affected app/version, and verified evidence. Distinguish app-level rejection from account-level suspension; only draft a factual appeal if there is evidence and a specific policy basis. Do not invent claims and recommend counsel for complex account/legal issues.
